answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks. An adversarial sybil cluster is separated by a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits probability flow from honest nodes, while min-cut transitivity bounds its aggregate stationary voting weight. Consequently, a terrace, glacier, or yarrow-themed identity cannot gain influence by multiplying colluding vertices: voting power requires attestations from well-connected honest regions.
